description:
s473u member 2 (2026-09-08): ONE PERSISTENT TRANSPILE SERVER PER TEST PROCESS.

The gate makes ~3200 `pl2cl` spawns and each costs 0.13 CPU-s of perl + PPI +
every Pl::* module BEFORE it reads a byte of the snippet -- ~420 CPU-s of a
2900 CPU-s run, paid over and over on inputs of a few dozen characters (#1544).

=== DONE (s473u) ===

SHAPE.  `Pl/t/PCLCore.pm` names a socket per TEST PROCESS in PCL_XSERVER (a
File::Temp dir, CLEANUP on); the first `pl2cl` that finds the variable starts
ONE already-loaded server there and every later call is a round trip.  Starting
it is LAZY -- a file that never transpiles pays nothing -- and the server ends
itself within a second of the owner dying (the `--server` liveness rule, s397).
The variable is inherited by everything a test file spawns, which is the point:
the `pl2cl --module --deps ...` calls the RUNTIME makes from inside an sbcl row
are served too.  `PCL_NO_SERVER=1` (or `PCL_XSERVER=`) is the old spawn path,
one variable away.

THE CLIENT is a BEGIN block ABOVE the `use Pl::Parser` chain in pl2cl, so a
served request never pays the module load at all; what is left is perl's own
start plus one round trip.  It DECLINES rather than guesses -- the ordinary path
is always correct, so declining is free and guessing is not: --server/--xserver/
--bundle/--executable/--help, the stdin forms (--output/--eval-pkg and bare
stdin: deciding whether pl2cl would READ stdin needs the option spec, and
reading it wrongly blocks on a pipe nobody closes), the per-process memory cap
variables, and any argv it cannot classify without re-implementing GetOptions.
It serves exactly one shape: one non-flag argument that is an existing file,
with `--deps FILE` the one value-taking option it understands.  A guard row
holds that list against pl2cl's own GetOptions `=s` declarations, so a new
value-taking option cannot silently be read as the source file.

THE STATE QUESTION, ANSWERED ONCE INSTEAD OF PER VARIABLE: the server FORKS A
CHILD PER REQUEST from a process that has never transpiled, so a request begins
from exactly the module state a freshly spawned pl2cl has -- the renamed-lexical
counters, the announce-once hashes, Pl::Environment, all of it.  An enumeration
of things to reset would drift the first time a counter is added; a fork cannot.
The child re-runs the SAME GetOptions on the request's argv (option parsing and
the command-line body were made subs, `_parse_options` / `_run_cli`, so a flag
cannot mean something different over a socket than on a command line).

THE SOCKET NAME is FNV-1a over the interpreter, the script's absolute path and
every PCL* / PERL5LIB assignment.  The environment is in the key because a
variable read at MODULE-LOAD time (Pl::Passes reads PCL_FACTS there) cannot be
answered by a server started under a different one; the SCRIPT PATH is in it
because PCL_XSERVER is inherited by everything a test file spawns, and some of
those run a pl2cl from another tree (an installed copy, a `git archive`
extraction) -- that one must get its own server, never this one's answers.

THE FAILURE CONTRACT (the resume brief's step c), all guarded:
  * a server that DIES mid-file is RECOVERED from: the next client finds a
    stale socket, starts a fresh server and answers identically.  Quiet, because
    a recovery is not a fallback.
  * a server that cannot be STARTED writes `.warned` (O_EXCL: one stderr line
    per test process) and `.down` (later calls decline at once, so the 10 s
    start wait is paid ONCE rather than 3200 times -- without it a broken server
    is a hang in all but name).  The line says the run is CORRECT but slow: a
    fallback that DIED would turn a performance problem into a broken gate, and
    a SILENT fallback is the #324 drift itself.
  * PCL_XSERVER naming a MISSING DIRECTORY declines in 0.14 s, loudly: nothing
    can be started there and no marker can be written either.
  * PCL_XSERVER_TRIED stops the memory-cap re-exec (which sits BELOW the client
    block) from running the whole client block a second time -- measured before
    the fix as two 10 s waits and two warnings.
  * the reply carries the child's RAW wait status (protocol PCLXS2) and the
    client RE-RAISES a signal death as that signal, so a caller's $? says the
    same thing in both halves of its word on both paths (rule 12: no quiet
    substitution).  Its guard row must exec pl2cl DIRECTLY -- a shell reports a
    child's signal death as exit 143 on both paths, and the first version of the
    row read 143 twice and proved nothing.
  * a server LOSING the start race now ASKS before unlinking: the naive
    `unlink; bind` removed a LIVE sibling's socket and bound happily, leaving
    two servers with the second shadowing the first and no bind failure to
    notice it by.

ACCEPTANCE (the USER's bar, "see so this really works"):
  * BYTE A/B over 360 real files (perl-tests/*.t, lib/**/*.pm, Pl/t/*.t
    -- the biggest and strangest inputs there are): served stdout, stderr and
    exit status IDENTICAL to spawned, file for file.  360 files, 360 IDENTICAL, 0 DIFF.
  * TWO FULL GATES on the SAME tree, server on and PCL_NO_SERVER=1, compared row
    by row after normalising temp names: 229 files, 7780 rows each, the same 13 pclxs xs failures, and
    ZERO verdict differences.  The one textual difference is parser-leak-01.t
    row 2, whose DESCRIPTION embeds its own RSS measurement ("got 20 kB" vs
    "got 16 kB"); the assertion (< 1 MB) passes in both, and the number moves
    run to run on BOTH paths (12, 16, 24, 28 kB measured in four solo runs).
    That file uses Pl::Parser IN PROCESS and never spawns pl2cl.
  * NUMBERS: one full gate, same tree, same 229 files / 7780 rows, best of
    three each: server OFF 164.3 s wall / 1232.9 CPU-s, server ON **86.1 s wall
    / 394.7 CPU-s** = 1.9x wall, 3.1x CPU for the server alone.  Against the
    s473u BEFORE (472f17c8, 224/7720, quiet box: 463 s / 2933 CPU-s) the whole
    batch is 5.4x wall and 7.4x CPU.  Per file the transpile-heavy ones are
    2.8-3.3x (transpile-test-04 35.6 -> 10.7 s, misc-fixes-01 34.6 -> 11.1,
    transpile-test-01 31.3 -> 10.7); files dominated by sbcl runs are unmoved,
    which is the residue task #1546 names.
  * CI-green files all pass; `prove tools/t/install-pcl.t` 57/57 (an installed
    tree never turns the server on -- tools/install-pcl copies Pl/ but SKIPS
    Pl/t, so PCLCore is not there).
  * The sweep and the companion are OUT OF SCOPE: they transpile one file each
    and are not the constraint.

GUARD: Pl/t/gate-cost-01.t, 32 rows, 2.6 s, TAP byte-identical with the server
on and off (it makes its own socket dir when there is nothing to inherit, so the
two acceptance gates can be compared row for row); inverse-verified on a
`git archive 92d2eb74` extraction.


=== CI NOTE (s478, Fable, 2026-09-08) ===
The merge went RED on CI (perl 5.38) while every local gate (perl 5.40) was green: gate-cost-01.t row 16 compared the EXIT CODE of an uncaught die between the served and spawned paths, and perl defines that code as $!-dependent (2 on 5.38 from Getopt::Long, 255 on 5.40); the served child resets $! so it read 255 everywhere.  Fixed in pl2cl: the usage error is an explicit `exit 2` on every perl.  Found by running the gate INSIDE the install-matrix container (recipe: DECIDED s478).  The served-vs-spawned contract stands; a die exit code is never a thing two paths can be asked to agree on.
subject: One persistent transpile server per test process (pl2cl --xserver): the gate stops paying 0.13 CPU-s of module load per row, with a fork per request as the state answer
